questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Asia, but the countries i could visit was limited because of the partner universities, and i thought that South Korea had a lot of culture and interesting things that i could explore, and i expected a lot from their education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was the experience, the place and the people who made it a fantastic experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, you get a lot of emails from the university, however there is a lot of information. And before i was enrolled in the university it was really hard, because i had to find all the information myself, and it is a chaotic the university website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an oriantation in the beginning where we got a lot of information, but it was also a bit chaotic. Furthermore there is an organiation who deals with international students, that you allways can contact if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We had to make a student card, that in Korea also works as a credit card, so we had to sign a paper 12 times, and everything was in Korean, so actually didn't know what we signed. It worked well with credit card, but the proces and information about it was not that well explained. Furthermore we were over a 1000 exchange students, and we were devided into 8 groups, i was the last group so waited around for at least 1 1/2 hour, it wasn't structured that well.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The university suggets student housing around the university, and have linked a website. It is quite easy to find a place within 1 km radius of the university and there are many places, with good prices. I would recommend that instead of dorms, because it is more social and you have your own room and bathroom with shared kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It cheap and easier to get new friends. However there is allways a land lady or land lord. They are often quite sweet, but are there everyday for 12 hours more and less, and clean. The rules a quite strict, you connot drink alcohol, or bring people to your room or outsiders there. Many places also have monitoring, and will tell you if you don't behave well, but as long as you clean up after yourself and don't wear shoes inside. 
 But Korea is cheap, so you spent most time out drinking and eating with people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was long and chaotic. I got the registration quite late, first in march and i was told by Copenhagen university that i would get in within 1 month. I didn't so was really stressed about it. There was a lot of things to fill out, and i first new that i was accepted in June, which was a bit late compared to everyone else. 
At my host university it was easy enough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could write to some from Copenhagen university, who dealt with exchange student.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2 of the courses i wanted, and the other 2 i didn't get.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I takes a lot of time, but don't stress about it. You will be grateful once you've been accepted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Quite low. I was dissapointed. One of my courses my professor could barely speak english, and he just read aloud from his power point. And sometimes he switched to korean. The other where better with english, but i didn't learn a lot of knew things. There are few homeworks, and it's mostly lectures and not many assignments or exercises.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UCPH is a lot better, because we reflect more about what we learn and discuss it, and have exercises, where in Korea it was more that you blindly trust what your professor telles you because he is a professor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Geophysics, Environmental Geography, Urbanization and industrialization in East Asia, New Media.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Environmental Geography. It was interesting. However it is a freshman course, so i didn't learn anything new, because geography is my major, but for others i think it would be interesting. 
New Media, was different because we watched movies and talked about them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Changing flight ticket. And taxis sometimes, beacuse the metro stops going between 01-05

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cooking home was more expencive than expected, because vegetables was a bit expensive. Eating out and drinking, and seing museums and so on, was cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of sports, but not everything is available for foreigners, because they speak in Korean.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Karaoke

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside of Seoul and see more of the country. Go on hikes, there is a national park really close to Seoul. See different district in the city. Watch temples and so on. You should got to Busan and Jeju.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Difficult, mainly because of the language. Many are not good at or don't speak english.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I tried really hard, but i was difficult because many are shy or don't speak well english. So i gave up a bit. But the KUBA buddies are nice and good at english, and otherwise i think it is easier to get friends that you have classes with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
There is a bit of racism in the country towards foreigners. I didn't experience anything disturbing but i know people who have, but many are also approaching you and want to speak with foreigners. 
A challenging things, is that you should not speak loud or barely speak in public transport. Many korean are quiet in metro and buses, and will tell you to be quiet if you are loud.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get out of your comfort zone and socialize a lot especially in the beginning, it's important to get friends so you don't feel lonely when you are away, it's good find a balance between being social and by yourself. Make sure to experience a lot, times fly by so don't postpone things to much. Be open to another culture.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: nope

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It an experience i will have with me for life. And i am happy that i tried it in an environment that is to different from mine, i learned a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Halfway through i got homesick, and a bit tired of the culture and people in Seoul, but many experienced the same, so i just pushed through and talked with your friends and family. Furthermore there was the Itaewon crush where 162 people died, it was hard being there when something like that happen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was a really great experience that i don't regret at all.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
